320-english: Counts when the topic relates to the region.
321-program-description: A comprehensive interdisciplinary base for graduate or professional school, recommended before graduate work in fields like History or Political Science. Normally B+ (3.30) in program courses on top of CGPA 3.0.
321-complementary-courses-42-credits: With the Adviser: 12 in Spanish or Portuguese; 30 more on the region, at least 15 in one cluster (Literature and Culture; Economics, History and Political Science; Anthropology and Geography), which may include 6 of theory or methods.
322-program-description: Interdisciplinary study of the region, combined with another Arts discipline, seeing an adviser in each. Program GPA 3.30, CGPA 3.00.
322-complementary-courses-18-credits: No more than 9 courses in one field.
323-program-description: Texts and histories from a wide range of cultures, in three streams: literature and the arts; history, culture and society; philosophy and religion. Distribution rules cover levels, disciplines, regions and periods.

Also requires a language minor (not English), ideally a third language for non-native English speakers: Classics (Language), East Asian, German Language, Hispanic, Italian, Jewish Studies, French Language, WIMES, Russian or Scriptural Languages.
324-required-courses: Two courses reflecting on what a Liberal Arts education means today and on your experience.
324-complementary-courses-30-credits: 30 credits in one stream: at least 6 at 200 in the stream, 15 at 300+, 6 at 400+ (not language), at most 18 in one discipline.
Regions: 6 on Africa or Asia, 6 on Europe, the Americas or Australasia. Periods: 6 before 1500, 6 from 1500–1900. One course can meet both.
324-stream-1-literature-and-the-arts-inc: For literature and arts across borders and traditions. 6 from List A (introductory, take early) and 24 from List B (core and related). The Director may approve substitutes.
324-list-a-6-credits: Up to 6 credits of MUAR with the Director.
324-list-b-24-credits: Any non-language course at 200+ in ARCH, ARTH, CLAS, ENGL, FREN, GERM, HISP, ITAL, LLCU and RUSS, or in JWST's Biblical Studies and Hebrew and Yiddish literature. At most 9 from the extra list.
325-stream-2-history-culture-and-society: For history, culture and society across borders and traditions. 6 from List A and 24 from List B. The Director may approve substitutes.
326-list-b-24-credits: Any course at 200+ in HIST, POLI, SOCI and COMS. At most 9 from the extra list.
327-stream-3-philosophy-and-religion: For philosophy and religion across borders and traditions. 6 from List A and 24 from List B. The Director may approve substitutes.
327-list-b-24-credits: Any non-language course at 200+ in PHIL, RELG, CATH, ISLA and JWST, or POLI's Political Theory. At most 9 from the extra list. ENVR 203 is needed for ENVR 400.
328-required-courses-9-credits: Three courses reflecting on a Liberal Arts education and your experience.
328-complementary-courses-51-credits: 51 credits in one stream: at least 9 at 200 in the stream, 24 at 300+, 6 at 400+ (not language), at most 21 in one discipline, with the same region and period rules.
328-list-a-9-credits: Up to 9 credits of MUAR with the Director.
329-list-b-42-credits: Same departments as the Major's stream 1. At most 12 from the extra list.
330-list-b-42-credits: Any course at 200+ in HIST, POLI, SOCI and COMS. At most 12 from the extra list.
331-list-b-42-credits: Same as the Major's stream 3. At most 12 from the extra list. ENVR 203 is needed for ENVR 400.
332-program-description: Working Russian, to explore life and culture in the original. Equivalent competence can waive prerequisites at 300+. Expandable to the Major.
332-complementary-courses-18-credits: RUSS 215 isn't open after RUSS 210 and 211; RUSS 316 not after RUSS 310 and 311; RUSS 415 not after RUSS 411.
332-program-description-2: An add-on to area studies or humanities and social science programs, with no Russian required. Expandable to the Major.
332-complementary-courses-18-credits-2: At least 6 from Group A, 6–12 from Group B. LLC courses may count with approval.
333-program-description: Language, literature and culture from the 19th century on, in Russian and in translation. Approved exchange and immersion credits can transfer.
333-group-a-russian-language-18-credits: With prior Russian, you may swap for Groups B or C with permission. Same exclusions for RUSS 215, 316 and 415.
334-program-description: For graduate study or advanced careers. CGPA and program GPA 3.00. Approved exchange credits transfer. Replace lower courses if competent. Up to 6 credits from other departments, LLC encouraged. See an adviser regularly. A minor elsewhere is required.
334-group-a-required-courses-12-credits: Propose reading or research courses by March 15 or November 15 of the term before.
334-group-b-russian-language: With prior Russian, you may swap for Groups C or D.
335-group-e-llc-and-faculty-of-arts: Check prerequisites and availability with the offering department. LLC options need approval.
335-program-description: Combine with another Arts discipline, with course approval from both first. CGPA and program GPA 3.00 or higher. Requirements are set individually with your adviser.
RUSS 490, usually in final year, is a thesis on Russian literature or culture, separate from your other program's. Propose by March 15 or November 15 of the term before.
336-group-c: Propose reading or research courses by March 15 or November 15 of the term before.
336-group-d-languages-literatures-and-cu: Check prerequisites and availability with the offering department.
338-about-linguistics: The scientific study of language: sounds, words, sentences, meaning, how languages are learned and processed, computational modelling, change over time, variation by region and identity, and data methods.

Prepares you for advanced work in linguistics, anthropology, cognitive neuroscience, computer science, philosophy and psychology, and careers in AI and speech technology, speech pathology, language revitalization, communication, teaching, translation and law.
Minor, major, honours and joint honours.
338-linguistics-related-program-minor-in: An option for those interested in cognition (p. 1165).
338-program-description: Basics across theoretical, experimental and computational linguistics, fieldwork and revitalization, variation and change. Expandable to the Major.
338-required-courses-9-credits: At McGill unless the Department agrees.
338-complementary-courses-9-credits: 6 at 300+, only 3 at 200. With LING 360, one of its prerequisites can count too.
339-program-description: Theoretical, experimental and computational linguistics, fieldwork and revitalization, variation and change.
339-complementary-courses-21-credits: 3 from the list; 18 LING chosen by interest, at least 9 at 400–500, only 3 at 200.
339-program-description-2: Breadth and depth across sub-areas, with an Honours Thesis in independent research.
Program GPA 3.30, B+ in three of LING 330, 331, 360 and 371 and in LING 480D, CGPA 3.00. First Class: CGPA 3.50 and A- on the thesis.
339-complementary-courses-39-credits: 3 from the list; 24 LING, 15 at 400–500, only 3 at 200.
